v01-el-celler-de-can-roca.name: El Celler de Can Roca
tags: Books ~11 months ahead, midnight on the 1st of the month; card to hold
Lunch — marginally easier to land than dinner
v01-el-celler-de-can-roca.why: Three Michelin stars, twice World's Best Restaurant (2013 & 2015), run by the three Roca brothers — Joan on the savoury pass, sommelier Josep on the wine, Jordi on pastry. Famous for an emotional, wine-led tasting that turns memory and landscape into courses. To order: the full tasting — the caramelised olives hung on a bonsai, the charcoal-grilled langoustine, and Jordi's perfume-derived desserts (aromas captured on a rotary evaporator). The real gatekeeper is the diary, not the door.
v01-el-celler-de-can-roca.hours: Lunch — marginally easier to land than dinner
v01-el-celler-de-can-roca.verdict: Forty years in, all three brothers are still on the floor — this is not a three-star coasting on its two world titles.
v01-el-celler-de-can-roca.signature: The full tasting: caramelised olives plucked from a bonsai, closing on Jordi's perfume-built desserts.
v01-el-celler-de-can-roca.caveat: Bookings open at midnight on the 1st of each month, eleven months out, card to hold; shut Sunday and Monday, and 16 August–1 September this summer.
v01-el-celler-de-can-roca.person: Ask for Josep — middle brother, raised in the family's Taialà bar; 50 Best's inaugural World's Best Sommelier in 2022, and he still works the room himself.

v02-restaurant-massana.name: Restaurant Massana
v02-restaurant-massana.why: One Michelin star since 2007, held through the 2026 Guide — a fourth-generation family kitchen led by Pere Massana. Famous for duck and, in winter, one of Girona's serious truffle menus. To order: the 'Homenaje al Magret de Pato', the duck breast on the card since 1986; the seasonal truffle tasting; the classic canelons. Quieter than Can Roca but still books days to weeks ahead.
v02-restaurant-massana.verdict: Girona's longest-held star after Can Roca's — kept since 2007, and bookable in days, not seasons.
v02-restaurant-massana.signature: Homenaje al Magret de Pato — duck breast off the grill, on the card since 1986.
v02-restaurant-massana.caveat: Shut Sunday and Monday, last tasting-menu seating at nine sharp — book days ahead, not on the night.
v02-restaurant-massana.person: Ask for Pere Massana Roger — second-generation chef; his father handed him the stoves in 2018, in the house his parents opened in 1986.

v03-divinum.name: Divinum
v03-divinum.why: One Michelin star, held in the 2026 Guide, in a below-street vault of the old Casino — the kitchen trained under Joan Roca. Famous for its cellar: a wine-driven, sommelier-led room. To order: the steak tartare finished at the table, and the wine-paired tasting menu. Below street level — easy to walk past; book a few days ahead.
v03-divinum.verdict: The only star in Girona won from the dining room, not the pass — Joan and Laura's floor, since the wine-bar days.
v03-divinum.signature: The classic steak tartare, mustard-cool, with whatever Laura pours against it.
v03-divinum.caveat: Shut Sunday and Monday, kitchen closes at ten — and the vault sits below street level, easy to march straight past.
v03-divinum.person: Ask for Laura Tejero — co-owner and sommelier; she has built the cellar since the 2001 wine-bar days on Carrer Argenteria.

v21-esperit-roca.name: Esperit Roca
v21-esperit-roca.neighborhood: La Fortalesa · Sant Julià de Ramis (10 km N)
tags: Go at lunch, for the views
v21-esperit-roca.why: One Michelin star since the 2025 Guide, held into 2026 — earned not for novelty but for how faithfully the Roca brothers' 1893 military fort above Girona serves El Celler's back catalogue — Toda la gamba (2012), Mar y montaña vegetal (2007), the Libro viejo dessert (2017) — rotating with the seasons. Famous as the family's grand project: an 80,000-bottle cellar beneath the dome, their own Esperit Roca distillery — now the kitchen's R&D space — a fifteen-room hotel and the CCR exhibition, ten kilometres north of the old town. To order: the Salty Spirit menu (€170), or the classics à la carte with a distillery pour. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday; dinner Thursday to Saturday only.
v21-esperit-roca.address: Castell de Sant Julià de Ramis, Muntanya dels Sants Metges, Carrer Major s/n, 17481 Sant Julià de Ramis, Girona
v21-esperit-roca.hours: Lunch Fri–Mon 13:00–14:30; dinner Thu–Sat 19:30–21:30; closed Tue–Wed. Holiday closure 3–11 Nov 2026; also closed 25 and 31 Dec 2026.
v21-esperit-roca.verdict: This is El Celler's back catalogue served under its own Michelin star — bookable ninety days out at €170, where the mothership takes eleven months and some €145 more.
v21-esperit-roca.signature: Toda la gamba — Palamós red prawn marinated in seaweed vinegar and katsuobushi; prawn velouté, sauce of the head, crisp legs, citric caviar, a concentrated distillate of the coral.
v21-esperit-roca.caveat: Not El Celler and not pretending to be — this is the archive, refined, not the frontier. You need a car or taxi up the hill from Girona; Tuesdays and Wednesdays are dark; dinner runs only Thursday to Saturday; and €139–170 before wine is real money for revival dishes.
v21-esperit-roca.person: Raül Sillero — head chef; eighteen years inside the Roca ecosystem, previously head chef of Mas Marroch, the family's events estate. His own framing: Esperit is "El Celler's library of dishes", not a last-minute outlet.

signal_chip.full: One MICHELIN star, first awarded in Guide España 2025 (gala 26 November 2024, Murcia — one of 32 new one-stars); retained in the 2026 Guide (gala Málaga, November 2025).
signal_chip.cosign: The star rewards fidelity of execution rather than novelty — which is precisely the offer, and why it holds.

v04-normal.name: Normal
v04-normal.why: The Roca brothers' deliberately plain room, interiors by Andreu Carulla — starred technique cooking everyday Catalan. Famous for doing tradition straight, no theatre. To order: the rotating market stew (escudella-style), the canelons, and whatever rice is on. The companion Bar Normal opens at noon for vermouth and all-day picking.
v04-normal.verdict: The Rocas at their most Catalan — their mother's home cooking by El Celler-trained hands, not a three-star spin-off doing tricks.
v04-normal.signature: The whisky tart with egg-yolk ice cream — the one dessert the inspectors single out.
v04-normal.caveat: Shut Mondays; the diary opens 90 days ahead at midnight, card down — €50 a head if you cancel inside three days.
v04-normal.person: Elisabet Nolla — head chef and director; El Celler-trained, handed the stoves by the Rocas at the 2021 opening.

v30-can-roca-taiala.name: Can Roca
v30-can-roca-taiala.why: The bar Josep Roca and Montserrat Fontané opened in 1967 in working-class Taialà, where the three Roca brothers grew up between the pans — 'the origin of everything', in their own words. It still runs as a casa de menjars: a short slate of firsts and seconds changing daily — spoon dishes, seasonal stews, rice on its appointed day, homemade desserts to close. The €18 menú (verified October 2025) feeds El Celler de Can Roca's own brigade at lunch — seventy-plus cooks and waiters daily, as hard a co-sign as cheap food gets. Weekday lunch only, two sittings; cross the Onyar and keep walking, it is a good 25 minutes north-west of the old town.
v30-can-roca-taiala.hours: Mon–Fri: bar 6:30–17:00, fork breakfasts 8:30–10:30, menú 13:00–15:30 in two sittings. Closed Sat–Sun.
v30-can-roca-taiala.verdict: The cheapest sit-down meal in the Roca universe — €18 buys lunch from the family kitchen that raised a three-Michelin-star dynasty, and the Celler's own brigade eats it daily.
v30-can-roca-taiala.signature: The menú's fish day — rap a la marinera, monkfish yielding under a dense marinera sauce that asks for bread.
v30-can-roca-taiala.caveat: A formica-and-telly neighbourhood bar half an hour's walk from the Barri Vell, weekday lunch only — go for the cooking and the story, not a sighting of the brothers; the menú has crept from €16 (2023) via €17 (spring 2025) to €18 (autumn 2025), and August closing is unverified, so ring 972 20 51 19 before crossing town.

v07-can-marques.name: Can Marquès
tags: Advisable for the three dinner nights
v07-can-marques.why: One of Girona's longest-running family tables, opened 1920 and now fourth generation. Famous for old-Girona home cooking off the market next door. To order: botifarra with melted brie; salt cod with samfaina and romesco; the daily rice. Night service Wed–Fri only (20:30–22:30); it shops Mercat del Lleó next door.
v07-can-marques.verdict: Four unbroken generations since 1920 — among Girona's longest-running tables, and the Mercat del Lleó next door still sets the menu.
v07-can-marques.signature: The Thursday rice — the pan carries whatever the market gave up that morning.
v07-can-marques.caveat: Lunch is the meal: dinner is Thursday and Friday only, groups only — and Saturdays shut mid-June to mid-September.
v07-can-marques.person: Ask for Eugeni Sánchez Marqués — fourth generation; his great-grandparents kept a boarding house here before the Mercat del Lleó was even built.

v08-casa-marieta.name: Casa Marieta
v08-casa-marieta.neighborhood: Barri Vell · Plaça de la Independència
v08-casa-marieta.why: On the arcaded Plaça de la Independència since 1892, five generations in. Famous for the terrace and unbudging Catalan classics. To order: duck with pears, baked lamb shoulder, and the canelons. Also does takeaway if the room is full.
v08-casa-marieta.verdict: Girona's oldest restaurant — on a square ringed with look-alike terraces, the one that has cooked here since 1892 and still cooks like it.
v08-casa-marieta.signature: Duck with pears: the old Catalan way, pears gone amber in the roasting juices.
v08-casa-marieta.caveat: Open daily but on rails — lunch 12.30 to 3.30, dinner 7.30 to 10.30, half an hour longer at weekends, nothing between; the arcaded terrace books out first, and nobody here is chasing tasting-menu invention.

dishes.name: Xuixo de Girona

v09-fonda-cal-ros.name: Fonda Cal Ros
v09-fonda-cal-ros.neighborhood: Barri Vell · Carrer de la Cort Reial
v09-fonda-cal-ros.why: A historic inn under stone vaults, relaunched by Marc Gascons and the Michelin-starred Els Tinars team. Famous for market cooking with a refined hand. To order: whatever the weekly market menu carries — expect a rice, a seasonal fish, a slow-cooked meat. Closed Tue; on the very street where the xuixo was born.
v09-fonda-cal-ros.address: Carrer de la Cort Reial 9, 17004 Girona
v09-fonda-cal-ros.verdict: Not the Gascons' starred table — the same Els Tinars hands cooking fricandó and rice a la llauna for fonda money under the old inn's vaults.
v09-fonda-cal-ros.signature: Rockfish rice a la llauna — baked flat in its tin until the edges catch.
v09-fonda-cal-ros.caveat: Shut Tuesdays and Wednesdays — not the Monday you'd guess; plates land to share, so order as a table, not as individuals.
v09-fonda-cal-ros.person: Elena Gascons — she runs the room; brother Marc, on the stoves, has held Els Tinars' Michelin star since 2008.

v31-dit-i-fet.name: Dit i Fet
v31-dit-i-fet.why: Adrià Edo (kitchen) and Júlia Trota (room) both came out of El Celler de Can Roca before opening this tight seasonal bistro on Carrer dels Calderers, under the shadow of Sant Feliu. Joan Roca names it as his place to eat in his own town — 'it's run by people who had worked with us' — and the 2026 Michelin Guide lists it. The register is Girona product with Celler-trained precision at bistro money: oxtail croquettes, a barely-set Palamós prawn tortilla, cap i pota for the brave, and the city's own xuixo pastry finished on the grill. Kitchen 13:00–15:00 and 20:00–22:30, closed Tuesday and Wednesday — book ahead.
v31-dit-i-fet.verdict: Joan Roca's named pick to eat out in Girona — ex-Celler craft at €40–50 a head, and the 2026 Michelin Guide agrees it belongs on the map.
v31-dit-i-fet.signature: ★ Tortilla cremosa de gamba de Palamós — a barely-set omelette running with Palamós red prawn, the coast folded into eggs (€24).
v31-dit-i-fet.caveat: Closed Tuesday and Wednesday and the secret is out — reserve. At €40–50 a head it sits at the dear end of 'casual', and the short seasonal card means a dish you read about may have rotated off.

dishes.name: Tortilla cremosa de gamba de Palamós

v32-safo.name: SAFO
v32-safo.neighborhood: Barri Vell — by Plaça del Vi
v32-safo.why: Chef Marietta Richter — born in Kenya to a Mexican father, trained through La Pubilla and Gresca in Barcelona — and sommelier Víctor Martín opened this natural-wine bar-à-vins beside Plaça del Vi in 2023: one page of share plates crossing Catalunya with Mexico and Kenya, and a cellar Martín talks you through glass by glass. Joan Roca vouches for it in the most neighbourly terms possible — 'not only our friends and neighbours, they also have very good natural wines. And you eat very well.' The pair took the emerging-chef Cuiner award at Gastronomic Forum Barcelona in 2024, and the cooking is playful and market-led: a crisp octopus quesadilla with avocado cream, a stracciatella galette with grilled bimi, whatever the week allows. In July and August it runs dinner only, Monday to Friday, 19:00 to midnight.
v32-safo.hours: Jul–Aug: Mon–Fri 19:00–24:00, dinner only · rest of year: Tue 20:00–24:00, Wed–Sat 13:00–16:00 & 20:00–24:00; kitchen 13:00–15:30 / 20:00–22:00 (official site, 2026)
v32-safo.verdict: Girona's most serious natural-wine room wearing its least serious face — vouched for, in print, by the three-star neighbour up the street.
v32-safo.signature: ★ Crispy octopus quesadilla with avocado cream — Richter's Mexico–Catalunya axis in a single bite.
v32-safo.caveat: July–August is dinner only, Monday–Friday — and the one-page menu changes constantly, so the dish you read about may be gone. Natural wine means funk: trust Víctor rather than asking for Rioja.

dishes.name: Crispy octopus quesadilla, avocado cream

dishes.name: Stracciatella galette with grilled bimi

dishes.name: Natural wine by the glass

v10-nu.name: Nexe
v10-nu.why: Nu until August 2022, when Pere Massana signed the room over to his own kitchen team — head chef Albert Izquierdo and second Hugo Cuenca reopened it as Nexe and have kept the MICHELIN Guide listing without him; Guía Repsol Recomendado 2026. Famous for cooking worked up at the open bar. To order: the steak tartare made in front of you, then the short market carte. Shut Sun & Mon; service 13:00–15:00 and 20:00–22:00 — book ahead.
v10-nu.verdict: Nu is gone — Massana signed the room over to his own cooks in 2022, and as Nexe they've kept their MICHELIN Guide listing without him.
v10-nu.signature: Steak tartare, worked up in front of you at the open bar.
v10-nu.caveat: Shut Sunday and Monday, two-hour service windows — book, and don't bank on the tasting menu TheFork advertises; the carte runs short.
v10-nu.person: Ask for Albert Izquierdo — Nu's last head chef under Pere Massana; he took the room over with Hugo Cuenca in 2022.
